title: Work IQ: policy-based governance of agents and their capabilities
summary: The roadmap facts and documented administrative paths and commands are supported; the cited pages opened successfully during this check. Two descriptive statements remain unsupported: that the policy layer consists of a single switch and that the access-control guide is preview documentation. The mutation-default wording should also acknowledge Microsoft's different statement for Copilot Studio.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans policy-based controls for administrators to govern agents and their capabilities at scale.
claims.quote: Provide administrators with policy-based controls for governing agents and their capabilities at scale.

claims.claim: That sentence is the full description supplied by the roadmap item.
claims.quote: "description": "Provide administrators with policy-based controls for governing agents and their capabilities at scale."

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP tenant policy settings are at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Agents > Tools. In the tools registry, select Work IQ MCP. On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.claim: An API or automation operation that turns Work IQ MCP tenant policy on or off is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "policy" "Microsoft Graph" "settings"; Work IQ MCP tenant policy enable default on off policy governance API Microsoft Graph PowerShell. Read MCP policy guide and relevant reference excerpts; configuration metadata is described, but no setting operation is documented.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls table
claims.claim: A Work IQ MCP policy change can take up to 24 hours to apply across the tenant.
claims.quote: After you save the setting, it can take up to 24 hours for the policy change to apply across your tenant.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The MCP policy guide says mutation operations, including create, update, delete and sending email, are disallowed by default.
claims.quote: By default, mutation operations aren't allowed for safety. This restriction includes create, update, delete, and action requests that modify data, such as sending email.
claims.fix: Keep the attribution to the MCP policy guide and add: 'The Copilot Studio Work IQ guide separately says write operations are on by default, subject to organizational permissions and policies; check the applicable experience rather than assuming a uniform write default.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/add-work-iq#work-iq-key-features, which states 'Write operations are on by default. Your organization's permissions and policies still apply.'

claims.claim: Access to Work IQ MCP is a condition to check when the Policy tab is unavailable.
claims.quote: If you don't see the Work IQ MCP policy settings, check that your tenant has access to Work IQ MCP and that your admin account has the required permissions.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The policy guide requires an account permitted to manage tenant-level Work IQ or Copilot settings.
claims.quote: Sign in with an account that has permission to manage tenant-level Work IQ or Copilot settings.

claims.claim: The Policy tab guide itself names no built-in administrator role.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP policy governance tenant policy Rego mutation default admin center. Read Policy governance for Work IQ MCP in full; its account requirement is permission to manage tenant-level Work IQ or Copilot settings, with no named built-in role.

claims.claim: The tenant-wide Work IQ MCP server can be blocked at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Block.
claims.quote: This control applies to the entire Work IQ MCP server, separate from Copilot audience settings or App Access. Select Agents > Tools. Select Work IQ MCP. To block access to the server, select Block.

claims.claim: An API or automation equivalent of the Work IQ MCP server Block control is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP server block access Microsoft Graph API tools registry; "Work IQ MCP" "Block" "API". Read access-control guide and registry-management excerpts; no equivalent operation was found. The Graph MCP Server for Enterprise disable endpoint documents a different server.

claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "enable" "Entra admin center" service principal. Read Enable your tenant for Work IQ and relevant Foundry setup excerpts; the documented 'Admin center' procedure actually sends a POST in Graph Explorer, not an admin-center navigation setting.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/servicePrincipals with appId fdcc1f02-fc51-4226-8753-f668596af7f7 provisions Work IQ for the organization.
claims.quote: Set the method to POST and the URL to https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals. Enter the following in the Request body. { "appId": "fdcc1f02-fc51-4226-8753-f668596af7f7" }
claims.fix: Set controls[2].api.call and the rendered call to 'POST /v1.0/servicePrincipals'. Add to the row note: 'The request body sets appId to fdcc1f02-fc51-4226-8753-f668596af7f7.' Keep the Azure CLI alternative.

claims.claim: az ad sp create --id <appId> is an alternative for creating the Work IQ service principal.
claims.quote: Create the Work IQ service principal in your organization by running the following command. az ad sp create --id fdcc1f02-fc51-4226-8753-f668596af7f7

claims.claim: Consent is granted at Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > App registrations > app > API permissions > Grant admin consent for [your tenant].
claims.quote: Grant consent: In the Microsoft Entra admin center, go to Entra ID > App registrations > select the app > API permissions. Select Grant admin consent for [your tenant].

claims.claim: On that app's API permissions page, selecting WorkIQAgent.Ask > Revoke admin consent revokes consent.
claims.quote: Revoke consent: On the same API permissions page, select the WorkIQAgent.Ask permission and select Revoke admin consent.

claims.where: controls[3].api; Governance controls table; Governance controls: final paragraph
claims.claim: az ad app permission admin-consent --id <appId> grants the application's requested permissions through admin consent.
claims.quote: Add the WorkIQAgent.Ask delegated permission and grant consent. az ad app permission admin-consent --id $APP_ID

claims.where: controls[3].note; Governance controls table; Governance controls: final paragraph
claims.claim: The application must request WorkIQAgent.Ask before the documented consent operation.
claims.quote: Select WorkIQAgent.Ask and then select Add permissions. Select Grant admin consent for [your tenant]. Review the confirmation dialog and select Yes.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Governance controls table; Governance controls: final paragraph
claims.claim: The quickstart adds the WorkIQAgent.Ask permission with az ad app permission add before running admin-consent.
claims.quote:
az ad app permission add --id $APP_ID --api fdcc1f02-fc51-4226-8753-f668596af7f7 --api-permissions "0b1715fd-f4bf-4c63-b16d-5be31f9847c2=Scope"
az ad app permission admin-consent --id $APP_ID

claims.claim: Work IQ uses a Rego-based policy layer.
claims.quote: The policy layer uses Rego, the policy language from Open Policy Agent (OPA), to express authorization rules.

claims.where: What's changing: third paragraph; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The policy layer applies request-time restrictions to resource paths accessed by Work IQ MCP tool requests.
claims.quote: It adds a request-time governance layer that can allow or deny specific MCP tool requests based on tenant policy. Data access scope: Which Microsoft 365 resource paths MCP tools can access.

claims.where: What's changing: third paragraph; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Policy can restrict the operations and capabilities used by Work IQ MCP requests.
claims.quote: For example, a tenant policy can allow read access to common productivity data while blocking high-risk paths, write operations, or large collection traversal.

claims.claim: The policy layer can govern data retrieval by Work IQ MCP requests.
claims.quote: Data retrieval limits: Whether collection reads are bounded to reduce large-scale data extraction risk.

claims.where: What's changing: third paragraph; Why it matters
claims.claim: Administrators can enable supported mutation scenarios through tenant policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Administrators can enable supported mutation scenarios through tenant policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center when those capabilities are needed.

claims.claim: The MCP policy guide does not link its documented controls to roadmap item 570652.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ policy existing agents retroactive Agent 365 roadmap 570652; Work IQ agent policy governance licensing price governance control. Read MCP policy guide in full and roadmap; no link identifying the documented surface as item 570652 was found.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls: first paragraph after table; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy cannot grant access beyond the signed-in user's existing Microsoft 365 permissions.
claims.quote: Policy can't grant access beyond what the signed-in user is already allowed to access.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Initial Work IQ MCP policy control is tenant-wide and can be turned on or off by tenant administrators.
claims.quote: In the initial release, Work IQ MCP provides tenant-level policy control. In the Microsoft 365 admin center, tenant administrators can turn Work IQ MCP policy on or off for the tenant.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls: first paragraph after table
claims.claim: Per-user, per-app, per-agent and scenario-specific policy templates are not part of the initial policy surface.
claims.quote: Tenant-level control applies across the tenant. Per-user, per-app, per-agent, or scenario-specific policy templates aren't part of the initial policy control surface.

claims.claim: The tenant-enablement guide requires a Global Administrator for one-time Work IQ setup.
claims.quote: A user with Global Administrator role for the one-time Work IQ setup

claims.claim: Enabling tenant-wide request-time MCP policy can cause existing callers' requests to be denied.
claims.quote: When you turn on the policy, it applies across the tenant and helps control MCP tool access at request time. An MCP request can fail because of tenant policy even when the user is authenticated and the app has the required OAuth permission.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls: first paragraph after table
claims.claim: Learn describes policy-denied responses as governance decisions rather than transient failures to retry.
claims.quote: Treat policy-denied responses as governance decisions, not transient failures to retry automatically.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Retroactive evaluation or remediation of already-created agents is not described for this planned change.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ MCP" "policy" "retroactive"; Work IQ policy existing agents retroactive Agent 365 roadmap 570652. Read roadmap, MCP policy guide and relevant Work IQ and Agent 365 excerpts; they describe request-time enforcement, not retroactive agent evaluation or remediation.

claims.claim: The roadmap item itself names no licence, add-on or meter.
claims.quote: Provide administrators with policy-based controls for governing agents and their capabilities at scale.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance controls: final paragraph; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Work IQ API use is metered through a consumption-based model using Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: You pay for use of the Work IQ API through a consumption-based model that uses Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: A separate price for the planned governance control is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ agent policy governance licensing price governance control. Read roadmap, MCP policy guide, Work IQ overview, tenant-enablement prerequisites, Copilot Studio Work IQ guide and Plan licensing and cost; no separate governance-control price was found.

claims.where: Governance controls: first paragraph after table
claims.claim: In the initial release the policy layer is a single tenant-level switch.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "policy" "Microsoft Graph" "settings". Read MCP policy guide in full; it documents on/off, supported mutation configuration and toggle-style and numeric settings, but does not say the layer consists of one switch.
claims.fix: Replace 'In the initial release the policy layer is a single tenant-level switch' with 'In the initial release, Work IQ MCP policy control is tenant-level'.

claims.where: Governance controls: first paragraph after table
claims.claim: More granular policy controls and templates are described as possible later additions, not current capabilities.
claims.quote: More granular controls and policy templates might be added later based on customer requests, feedback, and usage.

claims.where: Governance controls: first paragraph after table
claims.claim: Application-specific consent provides finer access governance alongside the signed-in user's permissions.
claims.quote: As an Entra admin, you control which applications in your tenant can access Work IQ data on behalf of users. Admin consent for WorkIQAgent.Ask is required before any user in your organization can authenticate through the app.

claims.claim: Spending policies can include or exclude Work IQ API.
claims.quote: Include Cowork and exclude Work IQ API from a policy when its users shouldn't consume credits through Work IQ API. Review all applicable policies, including the default policy. Excluding a service from one policy doesn't exclude it from other policies.

claims.claim: Spending policies can set consumption limits for covered services and users.
claims.quote: Set policy and per-user limits: Limit monthly consumption for selected user groups and the services covered by their policies.

claims.claim: Spending policies do not reserve credits for a workload, user or group.
claims.quote: Spending policies control access and spending limits; they don't reserve or allocate credits for a workload, user, or group.

claims.claim: The linked Copilot Credits setup guide documents general spending-policy setup.
claims.quote: Use the Cost Management dashboard in the Microsoft 365 admin center to enable usage-based billing, activate the default spending policy, create identity-based and resource-based spending policies.
